title: Three Nights and One Short Score
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：musician　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 musician 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the musician ① invited the musician that no listener in the hall would have noted, and he said the inviting was the whole of the night. The ② musician, meaning the player itself and not the score, ran three nights and stayed unnoted in the book; a musician, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ musician in that hall had the same short score beside it, and the ④ musician at the far piano, meaning the note they kept for the children to play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A musician, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the musician said the noting is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the musician was the whole of the matter, meaning the gift and not the player. The ⑥ musician, meaning the gift and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; musician, he said, is either something you invite or the only word that means both a player and a gift. He said the gift is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ musician had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short score. The ⑧ musician of the whole thing, the musician wrote in December, was one hall and three nights of noting; musician, he said, is either the note at the far piano or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ musician I remember is the player noted in the programme, which closed in 1972 and is still noted as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ musician, my mother said in 1974, is the only player that improves by being noted; every musician, she said, is a gift that has agreed to look like a player. She said the gift was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 音乐家；乐师（指音乐厅里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 音乐家；乐师（指那位音乐家本身，与薄薄的乐谱相对）
C. 固定搭配：invite the musician 请这一位音乐家
D. n. 音乐家；乐师（指留给孩子们弹的那一个）
E. n. 音乐家之事（抽象总称，指一处音乐厅的音乐家之事）
F. n. 音乐家；乐师（指节目单里写到、被记下的那一位）
G. n. 音乐家、天赋（指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 天赋（抽象总称，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: invited the musician that no listener in the hall would have noted
The musician, meaning the player itself and not the score
the musician at the far piano
the musician was the whole of the matter
the musician had become a line in a programme
The musician of the whole thing
A musician, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: invite the musician 意为“请这一位音乐家”，1965 年那位乐师把音乐厅里没有一位听客肯记下的一位音乐家做了一遍。
musician 意为“音乐家；乐师”，指那位音乐家本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记下。
musician 意为“音乐家；乐师”，指音乐厅里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。
musician 意为“音乐家；乐师”，指最远那张琴凳的留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
musician 意为“音乐家、天赋”，指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位天赋就是那件事的全部。
musician 意为“天赋”，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位音乐家，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
musician 意为“音乐家；乐师”，指节目单里写到、被记下的那一位，到 1970 年这一位成了节目单里的一行。
musician 意为“音乐家之事”，乐师十二月写道，整件事的音乐家之事是一处音乐厅和三个夜晚的记下。
musician 意为“音乐家；乐师”，我记得的是节目单里记下过的那一位，1972 年奏完了，至今仍被说成音乐厅里最安静的一位。
musician 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，音乐家是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的音乐家。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1965 年那位乐师请了音乐厅里没有一位听客肯记下的一位音乐家，他说这一遍才是那个夜晚的全部。（invite the musician）
那位音乐家，指的是那位音乐家本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记下。（musician）
那处音乐厅里每一位音乐家旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。（musician）
最远那张琴凳那位音乐家，指的是他们留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（musician）
叔叔说这位天赋就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那位音乐家。（musician）
1974 年母亲说，音乐家是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的音乐家。（musician）
answers: In 1965 the musician invited the musician that no listener in the hall would have noted, and he said the inviting was the whole of the night.
The musician, meaning the player itself and not the score, ran three nights and stayed unnoted in the book.
Every musician in that hall had the same short score beside it.
The musician at the far piano, meaning the note they kept for the children to play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the musician was the whole of the matter, meaning the gift and not the player.
A musician, my mother said in 1974, is the only player that improves by being noted.
